node.title: Re: Knowing when a code string contains code that will be executed at compile-time/end? (updated)
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
I am given a code string by user, and wants to know if the code contains statements or special blocks that are executed not in regular run time.

Impossible with a static parse (Update: the classic links on "only perl can parse Perl": [id://44722] and [id://663393], and [tye]'s reply to the latter). Consider for example eval(uc('end').'{...}') or something more convoluted, like variations on s s s END { ... } see (Update 3: like s x x qq s \Uens.'D{...}' xexe).

The only way to do this safely is to limit the user to a subset of Perl that is statically parseable. See the new module [mod://standard] and Sawyer's recent [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=sTEshbh2lYQ|talk] on it.

Update 2: As [LanX] [id://11120770|points out], [mod://B::Deparse] is not perfect, and using [mod://standard] unfortunately doesn't protect you from those issues either. It would be possible to keep both the original [mod://standard]-conforming string (checked to ensure it doesn't contain any BEGIN, eval, do, use, and so on) and its [doc://eval]ed coderef, e.g. in an object that could overload stringification and coderef-dereferencing, but that might be overkill depending on what you're trying to do.
